long_description:
Āio: a Puoro Māori Sound Journey
Journey inward through Māori sound, pūrākau and crystal bowls, creating a peaceful evening of deep listening, rest and restoration.

About this Event


Āio: a Puoro Māori Sound Journey




Starts at 6pm

Experience a peaceful Māori sound journey blending taonga pūoro, story, and crystal bowls for deep relaxation and inner calm

“Āio” speaks to peace and inner calm. In this immersive evening, pūrākau, taonga pūoro and waiata are woven together with the healing vibrations of crystal singing bowls, creating a space for deep listening, rest and restoration.

The organic tones of traditional Māori instruments including kōauau, pūtōrino, porotiti and pūtātara blend with the resonance of crystal bowls, chimes and ukulele, inviting you to slow down, soften and reconnect with your wairua and body. Through story, sound and vibration, this is a gentle journey inward.


What to bring:

Yoga mats, blankets and cushions will be provided, but you are welcome to bring extra for comfort!









After the sound journey, share in a nourishing plant-based dinner and dessert, included in your ticket, a warm way to close the evening together.





Meet your hosts & musicians: Smita, Peter, and Alexandra:

Smita (Ngāi Te Rangi) was born and raised in Aotearoa. From a young age she was drawn to music as a means for reflection and self-expression. During her music studies at university, she was introduced to taonga pūoro, and this sparked a personal journey of reconnection to te ao Māori and her own whakapapa. Following university, she lived in an ashram for several years where she was introduced to the wonderful practice of bhakti yoga. She now lives with her husband in the Wellington region, where they regularly participate in kirtan (mantra music meditation) at Bhakti Lounge.

Peter is Pākehā, with grandparents from England and Ireland, and has been on a four-year journey learning the art of taonga pūoro — the traditional Māori musical instruments of Aotearoa. Guided by the wisdom and generosity of expert makers and players, he has learned both to craft and to play these unique instruments. For Peter, taonga pūoro offer a way to connect deeply with sound, story, and the natural world, and he is excited to share their voices as part of this sound bath experience.

Alexandra is a sound healing practitioner devoted to nurturing healing in both mind and body. She believes that sound vibration holds the power to expand consciousness and restore harmony and balance in our lives. Her journey into sound healing began with the realization of how deeply sound vibration was affecting her psyche, making her more mindful of the music she listens to and the intention it carries. Along the way, she has drawn inspiration from artists such as Deva Premal, The Flying Mystics, Stevin McNamara, and the Bhakti Lounge Kirtan. Their music has profoundly influenced her own sound healing practice, inspiring her to explore sound as a tool for transformation, connection, and inner peace.

Join Business Central and the Wellington Chamber of Commerce for an exclusive breakfast event featuring Prime Minister Rt Hon Christopher Luxon in conversation with Hayley Horan, Chief Executive of Business Central.

Készen állsz arra, hogy eljuss a világ egyik legvadabb és legérintetlenebb tájára? Az Új-Zéland kiscsoportos körutazás – kalandtúra a világ végén azoknak szól, akik nem csak látni szeretnének, hanem valóban átélni akarják a természet erejét és változatosságát. Utunkat az Északi-sziget különleges világában kezdjük: Auckland, Hobbiton, Rotorua és Wai-O-Tapu gejzírmezői, gőzölgő hőforrásai és vulkáni tájai már az első napokban megmutatják Új-Zéland nyers arcát. A Lake Taupō partján haladva érkezünk meg a Tongariro Nemzeti Parkba, ahol drámai vulkáni panorámák és alpesi környezet vár ránk — itt nem csak nézelődünk, beleállunk az élménybe. We’re Weird for Other Reasons is a world-first theatre show entirely created by members of New Zealand’s ace/aro/aspec community. Offered by Dr James Wenley (Te Herenga Waka-Victoria University of Wellington) and the team behind We’re Weird for Other Reasons', this workshop will involve playful prompts and exercises for us to connect and share in community.

Audio Description is available at all performances, with a touch tour offered 30 minutes before each performance. Please email to let us know you’re attending.

AR Monthly Concert - Laldy and Owen Hugh
Laldy; Wellington-based fiddle player Rachel James and guitarist Donald James combine forces for one mission: to play folk and “gie i' laldy”, meaning to do something with gusto or great enthusiasm. With Welsh and Scottish roots, they are inspired by Scottish, Irish and Scandinavian music traditions.
Laldy brings to the stage a set which weaves together contemporary and traditional folk tunes and songs with original writing and arrangement. Playing a selection of sweet songs, modal grooves and traditional bangers, Laldy are a lively and danceable offering to the New Zealand folk and festival scene.
Owen Hugh - has been writing songs since he was 16 though it
took him 3 years of trying before writing a decent one. He has just remastered all his albums and they are available on sites such as YouTube, Spotify and Apple music. His music always touches the soul and contains Celtic, Rock Folk and Blues influences. He cut his teeth at folk clubs in NZ and the UK in the 90’s and has played Edinburgh Fringe Festival 4 yrs in a row as well as several festivals in UK. Once described in the American Press as a cross between “Billy Connolly and James Taylor”, be prepared to laugh and cry possibly at the same time. After a period of writer’s block he is now recording and road-testing new material.
Entry: $20/$15 for members. Cash only (no eftpos facilities). Note: The concert will be on the first floor, with access via stairs or the lift. (Yes, the lift is back in action!) You may have to press the button at the side of the door to gain access to the building.

About this Event



What can you do with a creative degree?

College of Creative Arts | Toi Rauwhārangi graduates go on to build incredibly varied and inspiring careers across the creative industries and beyond. While creative study is sometimes questioned for its “employability”, the reality is that Aotearoa New Zealand’s arts and creative sector contributes $17.5 billion to GDP and makes up 4.2% of the total economy.

So where do our Screen Arts, Commercial Music, Design and Fine Arts graduates really end up?

Join us for a candid panel with recent graduates from Massey University’s College of Creative Arts | Toi Rauwhārangi and hear the real story of life after study: how they found work, what that transition looked like, and how they’re using what they learned in the real world. From building creative businesses and freelance careers to working in agencies, education, the public sector, and creative roles, our graduates are forging all kinds of futures.

You’ll hear from people working as:

artists and makers
designers and screen creatives
musicians and creative entrepreneurs
freelancers, contractors and sole traders
business owners and educators
creatives working both inside and outside the traditional creative industries

They’ll share the opportunities, connections and experiences that shaped their journey during study and beyond — including the realities of getting started in today’s economy.

We’ve scheduled this event for the evening before Open Day so students and whānau can attend together, especially if daytime commitments or travel make it harder to join us during the day. If you’re visiting from out of town, it’s also a great way to make the most of your time in Wellington.

And if you want even more of the inside scoop on studying at Massey, check out All Access — our student-run YouTube channel, where current students share what life at Toi Rauwhārangi is really like. https://www.youtube.com/@AllAccessMCA

• KSW member: $110
• Non-KSW member: $120
• Transponder hire is free for the weekend – if you have your own kart transponder, bring it along but check with us first to confirm it'll work with our system!

Bike entries are limited to 42 total, with a firm cap of 21 per grade based on qualifying times.

Entries close 20 August – get in early to confirm your spot!

PLEASE read the Supplementary Regulations (linked in the entry form) before you rock up – they cover everything you need to know for this event!

Grids
Three wide, staggered rows, with 2m between the rear of the bike in front and the front of the bike behind.

Pits
Pit site allocation TBC closer to the time.

Officials for the weekend
Clerk of Course: Alysha Sands
Steward of Meeting: Dane Foster
Friday and Saturday night support crew (so far!): Georgia Lynn, Quentin, John Busby and Matt Clarke

We NEED an army of volunteers for both Friday and Saturday night! There will be lights on the track, sure, but we can't underestimate the safety risk of running at night! Does racing make you hungry? Or thirsty?
The Club Café will be serving dinner both nights plus snacks and drinks. Alcoholic drinks available after racing only.

Not a member?
If you're not a BRNZ, MNZ or KSW member you can still race! Reach out and we'll give you the info you need.

Don't wanna race but wanna watch?
Spectators are free to come along and enjoy the racing – everyone's welcome! Just keep your wits about you and stay safe around the track.

More info to follow closer to the event – keep an eye on this page!

See you there!

A Voyage to the Moon by Offenbach: A NZSM Opera Production
Classical Performance students from the New Zealand School of Music – Te Kōkī present four performances of Jacques Offenbach's delightful comic opera A Voyage to the Moon, directed by Sara Brodie with musical direction by Kathryn Mosley.

Performance dates:
Friday 4 September, 7:30pm
Saturday 5 September, 3:00pm & 7:30pm
Sunday 6 September, 3:00pm

Duration: 70 minutes
Venue: The Adam Concert Room
Tickets: On sale now via Eventfinda with student and concession discounts available!

Inspired by this year's space exploration milestones, including NASA's Artemis II mission, this production celebrates Offenbach's imaginative 1875 opera, which was a sensation in Paris, running for an impressive 185 consecutive performances during its first run.

Loosely based on Jules Verne's novel From the Earth to the Moon, A Voyage to the Moon takes audiences on a adventure filled with fantastical lunar landscapes, eccentric characters, and Offenbach's trademark comedic twists. The story follows King V'lan, his adventurous son Prince Caprice, and their companions—including Microscope and Rhombus—as they journey to the Moon, where they encounter Cosmos, Princess Fantasia, Flamma, and other curious inhabitants of the lunar world.

Directed by Sara Brodie, who also led last year's fantastic production of L'enfant et les sortilèges, the opera features vocal numbers performed in French with English surtitles. The spoken dialogue is presented in English, bringing the comedy vividly to life for contemporary audiences.

This production showcases the talents of students across the Classical Performance programme, with NZSM voice students performing all roles and in ensembles, and the NZSM piano students taking part as rehearsal pianists (répétiteurs) and playing for the performances. Musical direction is provided by Head of Collaborative Piano Kathryn Mosley, and the production is coordinated by Head of Classical Voice Jenny Wollerman.

Join us for an imaginative, entertaining, and truly 'out there' operatic adventure!

What happens when you're standing trackside as the world's fastest drivers hurtle past at 300 kilometres an hour?

Or when you're interviewing champions moments after victory, heartbreak or controversy?

Most of us only see the finished broadcast.

The highlights.

The interviews.

The polished moments on screen.

But behind every major sporting event are extraordinary stories, fascinating personalities and split-second moments that rarely make it into the final broadcast.

Join renowned motorsport broadcaster and storyteller Greg "Rusty" Rust for a lively and entertaining Learning Lunch packed with behind-the-scenes stories from a remarkable career spent at the heart of international sport and media.

From Formula One and MotoGP to Bathurst, the Winter Olympics and the Commonwealth Games, Greg has spent decades meeting extraordinary people and witnessing history unfold from the best seat in the house.

Expect humour, fascinating stories, unexpected insights and plenty of memorable moments from life behind the microphone.

Greg "Rusty" Rust is one of Australia and New Zealand's best-known motorsport broadcasters, presenters and commentators. Based in Hawke's Bay, Greg is also the host of the award-winning Rusty's Garage podcast.

Power Up Central Hutt
Come to the first of the new 2026 Power Up The Hutt information sessions in the Hutt Bowling Club, Myrtle Street on the evening of Thursday 29th October at 7:30pm.

Power Up the Hutt is a free five-part community event series bringing together Hutt Valley residents who want to cut their power bills, reduce their carbon footprint, and future-proof their homes.

New Zealand has reached an electrification tipping point — households can now save money and significantly reduce their emissions by switching their appliances and vehicles to electric. But knowing where to start can feel overwhelming.

These friendly, practical evenings — hosted by local volunteers with experience in electrification and drawing on the research of Rewiring Aotearoa — will walk you through the real options available right now: solar panels and home batteries, electric vehicles, heat pump hot water systems, induction cooking, and making the switch from gas to electricity.

Businesses, schools, or community organisations interested in electrification are also welcome. No jargon. No sales pitch. Just straight talk from your neighbours about what works, what it costs, and how to get started.

2026 Francis Gurry Lecture on Intellectual Property - WELLINGTON
"The Future of IP Dispute Resolution" by Sir Colin Birss, Chancellor of the High Court of England and Wales

About this Event




5.30pm | Pre-event refreshments
6.00pm | Public lecture




The Future of IP Dispute Resolution

The legal landscape is changing before our eyes. The advent of AI and digital assets, the internationalisation of dispute resolution, and the changing expectations of users, all pose challenges, and intellectual property has always raised issues of its own.

This lecture will examine the state of intellectual property litigation today in the wider context, consider where it needs to be in future, and look at how we need to adapt to meet the challenges.

The topics include the major legal problems in IP which will need to be addressed; the legal and practical impact of artificial intelligence; the importance of digital assets and tokenisation; and the emergence of alternative modes of resolving dispute resolution.






Colin Birss is the Chancellor (Head of the Chancery Division) of the High Court of England and Wales. Called to the English Bar in 1990, he practised intellectual property law. In 2010 he became judge at the Patents County Court (now IPEC), in 2013 he went to the High Court, and in 2021 to the Court of Appeal. He was Deputy Head of Civil Justice 2021-25, and appointed Chancellor in 2025. He sits in the Court of Appeal and in the High Court.

Can Electricity Markets Deliver the Clean Energy Transition?
A global perspective on investment, reliability, and the risks of getting it wrong.

About this Event



Three recent shocks to electricity markets - cheap renewables, declining storage costs, and the return of demand growth - have led some to conclude that electricity markets as we know them have run their course. Drawing on thirty years of restructured markets abroad, this presentation will argue that these developments actually strengthen the case for markets — and will explore what reliability means, and how it should be provided, in a greener electricity system.

Professor James Bushnell – Biography

Professor James Bushnell is a distinguished scholar whose research and policy contributions have helped shape modern understanding of electricity markets, energy regulation, and climate policy, making him one of the most influential voices in energy economics. He is an internationally recognised expert in energy economics, electricity markets, environmental policy, and industrial organisation.The event is being facilitated by ERGANZ and will be hosted at the Wellington offices of Russell McVeagh

Date and Time: Thursday 3 September, 4pm - 6pm @Russell McVeagh, 157 Lambton Quay, please join us for a drink and nibbles from 4pm, presentation to start at 4:30pm with a Q&A to follow.

name: Trip: Belmont Regional Park at Dry Creek Entrance
venue: Hebden Cres,Dry Creek Campsite, Haywards, Lower Hutt 5010, New Zealand, Lower Hutt
long_description:
Trip: Belmont Regional Park at Dry Creek Entrance
We will climb for 40 minutes up the 4WD Buchanans Road Tramping Track, passing Dendrobium cunninghamii, Earina autumnalis, Helichrysum lanceolatum and Metrosideros colensoi.

From there we’ll walk bait lines and informal unformed tracks for a 90-minute circuit of Syzygium maire (maire tawake, swamp maire). Botanising time will be additional to this. Bring good footwear and gaiters if you have them for waterlogged sites. There is one place with hip-stretching tall steps cut into soil. Areas can be slippery when wet. Hand ropes are beside steep mud steps. This is a 7.5km walk with moving time of around two and a half hours.

There is recent research on Syzygium maire in the Wellington region, published by the School of Biological Sciences at Victoria University. The authors highlight that we ‘need to identify refugia in accessible, albeit sometimes fragmented, habitat’ and recommend ‘leveraging human–nature interactions in areas to create, expand, and protect habitat for [this] rare species in a rapidly changing world’. Syzygium maire has a threat classification of Threatened-Nationally Vulnerable. The research illustrates the preferred habitat of Syzygium maire is waterlogged areas. Such areas are few and shrinking, both nationally and in Wellington region.

This trip will look at thriving Syzygium maire that have fruited and seeded in the rare wetlands below Boulder Hill. We’ll see Ramarama, Threatened – Nationally Critical, and Coprosma rubra, At Risk – Declining and over 100 other plant species observed on iNaturalist. These can be seen in a map view of the proposed quarry Overburden Disposal Area.

Ominously there’s a Fast-track proposal to turn this precious area into a quarry overburden disposal area. This has been reported on by Radio NZ. The Friends of Belmont Regional Park and Wellington Botanical Society have strongly opposed this. The Fast-track application is here.

Non-members are welcome to join, making it an excellent opportunity to explore this region’s native flora.

Meet: Dry Creek Carpark, Hebden Crescent, Kelson, Lower Hutt at 9.30am. This Carpark with toilets is a 10-minute walk from Manor Park Station on the Hutt Valley Line. Trains leave Wellington at 8.35am and arrive at Manor Park Station at 9.08am.

Leader: John Barnett, 021 063 1590,

Shea McAleese: The Evolution of a Four-Time Olympian
What does it take to perform on the world's biggest stage?

And perhaps more importantly, what happens when the cheering stops, the jersey comes off, and it's time to reinvent yourself all over again?

Join four-time Olympian and New Zealand hockey legend Shea McAleese for an inspiring Learning Lunch exploring the highs, challenges and lessons of a life spent pursuing excellence.

From a young Hawke's Bay athlete with a dream to representing New Zealand at four Olympic Games and four Commonwealth Games, Shea's journey offers a fascinating insight into commitment, resilience and what it really takes to perform at an elite level.

But this isn't simply a story about sport.

It's about leadership, teamwork, personal growth and learning how to evolve through different chapters of life.

Today, Shea works as an international coach and leadership mentor, helping individuals and teams perform at their best. Drawing on lessons from elite sport, he shares a practical and human perspective on building trust, developing culture and creating environments where people thrive.

Expect honest stories, valuable insights and a fascinating look behind the scenes of life as an Olympian, coach and leader.

Meet Shea 🎤

Shea McAleese is one of New Zealand's most celebrated hockey players and a proud son of Hawke's Bay. Over a 16-year international career he represented the Black Sticks 320 times, competing at four Olympic Games and four Commonwealth Games. Since retiring from international hockey, he has transitioned into international coaching and leadership development, working with elite teams and building a global following through his coaching platform, Inside Hockey.

long_description:
National Dog Database
Using the NDD to its full potential. Get hands-on and use realistic scenarios to explore and learn the functionality of the NDD website.

About this Event


Description

The National Dog Database went live 1 May 2006 and provides a countrywide overview of dog control in New Zealand.

It brings great benefits to the animal control industry including the ability to;

track classified owners and dogs
monitor the national infringement count of owners
look up out of district dog and owner details
locate dogs when only limited information is available;
and contribute accurate data to ongoing policy analysis.







Outline

Using the NDD training environment (it looks just like the live NDD system but contains fictional data), the NDD training workshop will explore the following areas:

Background – the history of the NDD project – from 2003 to present
TA Extracts – how information gets from your local system to the NDD and the feedback the NDD will give you as well as the different types of files you can send
Searching – how to get the best out of the search screen and how to interpret the results of your search
The ToDo List – what are errors, warnings, information and system notifications? Detailed discussion about what you need to do with them.
Automated and Manual Linking – National Duplicates – comparing dogs and owners that look similar but are in different districts, and how to manually search for other duplicates.
Security – passwords, adding new users or expiring old accounts, as well as the owner protected status.
Reports – what reports you can run and how to use them in your TA. Did you know there are 18 different kinds of reports that you can generate from the NDD and that you can use some of them to compare your TA’s data to a national summary?







Learning outcomes

With a focus on maintaining data quality, participants in the workshop will learn to use the NDD as a tool for animal control and further understand the importance of administrative roles at the local level. Following the completion of the NDD training workshop, NDD users will have the confidence to use the database to its full potential.







Audience

This course is suitable for managers, team leaders and users with animal control administrator responsibilities.







Prerequisites

To participate in the NDD training workshop you must be a registered user of the National Dog Database (employee or contractor). You are required to bring your own laptop.
